subject.title: [Bug] Incorrect Sandbox Bind Mount Parsing for Windows Relative Drive-Letter Paths

question: Should OpenClaw continue rejecting Windows drive-relative sandbox bind sources while fixing only the misleading parse/error, or intentionally add deterministic support for resolving them?
rationale: Current tests and schema define absolute sources as the supported security contract, while the issue requests new process-state-dependent resolution behavior at a host mount boundary.

options.title: Keep rejection, fix diagnostic
options.body: Parse `C:project` as the full source, retain the non-absolute rejection, and add focused parser and validation regression tests.

options.title: Design drive-relative support
options.body: Define deterministic Windows resolution semantics, security policy behavior, documentation, and live Docker proof before accepting these sources.

recommendation.title: Keep rejection, fix diagnostic
recommendation.body: Parse `C:project` as the full source, retain the non-absolute rejection, and add focused parser and validation regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This team owns the sandbox path validation boundary and is best positioned to decide whether the supported source-path contract should expand.
